title.raw: 卷一百二十八 周書19: 列傳八 王朴 楊凝式 薛仁謙 蕭愿 盧損 王仁裕 裴羽 段希堯 司徒詡 邊蔚 王敏 Volume 128 Book of Later Zhou 30: Biographies 8 - Wang Pu, Yang Ningshi, Xue Fenqian, Xiao Yuan, Lu Sun, Wang Renyu, Pei Yu, Duan Xiyao, Si Tubi, Bian Yu, Wang Min

sentences.zh: 王朴，字文伯，東平人也。

translations.literal: Wang Pu, styled Wenbo, was a native of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, whose style was Wenbo, came from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 父序，以朴貴，贈左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His father Xu, because of Pu's eminence, was posthumously granted Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Xu, on account of Pu's rise, was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 朴幼警慧，好學善屬文。

translations.literal: Pu in youth was quick-witted and clever, fond of study and skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Pu was exceptionally bright, devoted to learning, and adept at literary writing.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，擢進士第，解褐授校書郎，依樞密使楊邠，館於邠第。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han he passed the jinshi examination, left the commoner's dress and was appointed Collator, attached to the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Bin, and lodged at Bin's residence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Han reign era Qianyou he took the jinshi degree, entered service as Collator, and served under Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Bin, living as a guest in Bin's household.

sentences.zh: 是時漢室浸亂，大臣交惡，朴度其必危，因乞告東歸。

translations.literal: At that time the Han house was gradually falling into disorder and great ministers were at odds with one another; Pu judged that it would surely become perilous and therefore requested leave to return east.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court was then sliding into chaos and its leading ministers were feuding; Pu foresaw disaster and asked permission to go home to the east.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李業輩作亂，害邠等三族，凡遊其門下者，多被其禍，而朴獨免。

translations.literal: Before long Li Ye and his faction raised a disturbance, killing the three clans of Bin and the like; all who had frequented their gates mostly suffered that calamity, yet Pu alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Ye and his associates rebelled and wiped out Bin's clan and two related families; most who had associated with them perished, but Pu alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 國初，世宗鎮澶淵，朝廷以朴為記室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, when Shizong was stationed at Chanyuan, the court appointed Pu as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou dynasty, while the future Emperor Shizong held Chanyuan, the court named Pu his recorder.

sentences.zh: 及世宗為開封尹，拜右拾遺，充開封府推官。

translations.literal: When Shizong became Intendant of Kaifeng, he was appointed Right Reminder and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong became Intendant of Kaifeng, Pu was made Right Reminder and assigned as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，授比部郎中，賜紫。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was granted Director of the Bureau of Review and presented with purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong acceded, Pu was appointed Director of the Bureau of Review and awarded the purple robe of high office.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，世宗命朝廷文學之士二十餘人，各撰策論一首，以試其才。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year Shizong ordered more than twenty literary men of the court each to compose one policy essay to test their talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of his second year Shizong directed more than twenty learned officials at court each to write a policy essay as a test of their ability.

sentences.zh: 時朴獻《平邊策》，云：

translations.literal: At that time Pu submitted the "Strategy for Pacifying the Borders," saying:
translations.idiomatic: Pu then presented his "Strategy for Pacifying the Borders," which read:

sentences.zh: 唐失道而失吳、蜀，晉失道而失幽、并，觀所以失之由，知所以平之術。

translations.literal: Tang lost the Way and thereby lost Wu and Shu; Jin lost the Way and thereby lost You and Bing. Observing the causes by which they were lost, one knows the methods by which to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Tang lost the Mandate and with it Wu and Shu; Jin lost the Mandate and with it You and Bing. Study why they were lost, and you will know how to recover them.

sentences.zh: 當失之時，莫不君暗政亂，兵驕民困，近者奸於內，遠者叛於外，小不制而至於大，大不制而至於僭。

translations.literal: At the time of their loss, without exception the ruler was benighted and government chaotic, the armies arrogant and the people distressed; those near were treacherous within, those far rebelled without; what was small, uncontrolled, grew great, and what was great, uncontrolled, reached usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever such losses occurred, the ruler was benighted and government corrupt, armies overbearing and the people exhausted, courtiers treacherous at home and frontier lords in revolt abroad; minor disorders left unchecked swelled into major ones, and major ones into outright usurpation.

sentences.zh: 天下離心，人不用命，吳、蜀乘其亂而竊其號，幽、并乘其間而據其地。

translations.literal: All under Heaven turned their hearts away and men would not obey orders; Wu and Shu seized their disorder and stole their titles, You and Bing seized the interval and occupied their territory.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lost its cohesion and men would not obey; Wu and Shu exploited the turmoil to seize imperial titles, while You and Bing took advantage of the crisis to hold the northern territories.

sentences.zh: 平之之術，在乎反唐、晉之失而已。

translations.literal: The method of pacifying them lies simply in reversing the errors of Tang and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The art of pacification is simply to undo what Tang and Jin did wrong.

sentences.zh: 必先進賢退不肖以清其時，用能去不能以審其材，恩信號令以結其心，賞功罰罪以盡其力，恭儉節用以豐其財，徭役以時以阜其民。

translations.literal: One must first advance the worthy and dismiss the unworthy to clarify the age, employ the able and remove the incapable to examine talent, bind hearts with kindness, trust, and commands, reward merit and punish crime to exhaust their strength, be respectful, frugal, and economical to enrich the treasury, and levy corvée at the proper seasons to enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: First promote the worthy and remove the unworthy to purify the age; appoint the capable and dismiss the incompetent to judge talent rightly; win loyalty through kindness, trust, and clear orders; reward merit and punish wrongdoing so that all give their utmost; practice respect, frugality, and restraint to fill the treasury; and levy labor only at proper seasons so the people may prosper.

sentences.zh: 俟其倉廩實、器用備、人可用而舉之。

translations.literal: Wait until granaries are full, implements prepared, and men can be employed, then undertake the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the granaries are full, arms and equipment ready, and the people fit for service—only then strike.

sentences.zh: 彼方之民，知我政化大行、上下同心、力強財足、人和將和、有必取之勢，則知彼情狀者願為之間諜，知彼山川者願為之先導。

translations.literal: When the people of that region know that our civilizing influence is widely practiced, superiors and inferiors of one mind, strength abundant and wealth sufficient, harmony among men and harmony among generals, and a momentum of certain conquest, then those who know their conditions will wish to be spies for us and those who know their mountains and rivers will wish to be our guides.
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy's people see our government flourishing, court and army united, strength and wealth ample, soldiers and commanders in harmony, and an irresistible tide of conquest, those who know their secrets will volunteer as spies and those who know their terrain will volunteer as guides.

sentences.zh: 彼民與此民之心同，是與天意同，與天意同則無不成之功。

translations.literal: When the hearts of those people and these people are the same, that is to be of one mind with Heaven's intent; to be of one mind with Heaven's intent is to have no achievement that cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When their people's hearts align with ours, we align with Heaven's will; and where Heaven's will is with us, no undertaking can fail.

sentences.zh: 攻取之道，從易者始，當今吳國，東至海，南至江，可撓之地二千里。

translations.literal: The way of attack and seizure begins with what is easy; the present state of Wu extends east to the sea and south to the Yangzi, with two thousand li of territory that can be harassed.
translations.idiomatic: In conquest, begin with what is easiest: Wu today stretches from the sea in the east to the Yangzi in the south, offering two thousand li of vulnerable ground.

sentences.zh: 從少備處先撓之，備東則撓西，備西則撓東，必奔走以救其弊，奔走之間，可以知彼之虛實、眾之強弱，攻虛擊弱，則所向無前矣。

translations.literal: Harass first where their defenses are thin; if they prepare in the east, harass the west, if in the west, harass the east—they will surely rush about to save their weak points, and in that rushing one may know their emptiness and fullness and the strength and weakness of their forces; attack the empty and strike the weak, and there will be no direction in which one cannot advance.
translations.idiomatic: Strike first where their defenses are weakest; if they reinforce the east, harass the west, and if the west, harass the east—they will be forced to rush about putting out fires, and in that confusion you can learn their true strength and weakness; attack where they are hollow and strike where they are feeble, and nothing will stand in your way.

sentences.zh: 勿大舉但以輕兵撓之。

translations.literal: Do not mount a major campaign but only harass them with light forces.
translations.idiomatic: Do not launch a major invasion; use only light troops to harry them.

sentences.zh: 彼人怯，知我師入其地，必大發以來應，數大發則必民困而國竭，一不大發則我獲其利，彼竭我利，則江北諸州，乃國家之所有也。

translations.literal: Those people are timid; knowing that our army has entered their territory, they will surely mobilize on a large scale to respond; if they mobilize on a large scale several times, the people will surely be distressed and the state exhausted; if once they do not mobilize on a large scale, we gain the advantage; they exhausted and we advantaged, then the prefectures north of the Yangzi will be what the state possesses.
translations.idiomatic: They are a timid foe; once they see our troops in their territory they will mobilize heavily to meet us. Repeated large mobilizations will exhaust their people and drain their state; if even once they fail to mobilize, we profit. When they are spent and we gain, the prefectures north of the Yangzi will fall into our hands.

sentences.zh: 既得江北，則用彼之民，揚我之兵，江之南亦不難而平之也。

translations.literal: Once the north bank of the Yangzi is obtained, then using their people and displaying our army, the south bank of the Yangzi will not be difficult to pacify either.
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold the north bank, we can use their people and advance our armies; the south bank will then be easy to subdue.

sentences.zh: 如此，則用力少而收功多。

translations.literal: In this way effort is little and harvest of achievement is great.
translations.idiomatic: In this way little effort yields great results.

sentences.zh: 得吳，則桂、廣皆為內臣，岷、蜀可飛書而召之，如不至，則四面並進，席卷而蜀平矣。

translations.literal: Once Wu is obtained, Gui and Guang will all become inner subjects; Min and Shu can be summoned by flying dispatch, and if they do not come, then advancing on all four sides together, sweeping up, Shu will be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu subdued, Gui and Guang will submit as inner provinces; Shu can be summoned by urgent dispatch, and if it refuses, a converging attack from all sides will sweep it up in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀平，幽可望風而至。

translations.literal: When Wu and Shu are pacified, You may be expected to submit at the first wind.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu and Shu are pacified, You will likely submit at the first sign of our advance.

sentences.zh: 惟並必死之寇，不可以恩信誘，必須以強兵攻之，但亦不足以為邊患，可為後圖，候其便則一削以平之。

translations.literal: Only Bing is an enemy that must fight to the death; it cannot be enticed by kindness and trust and must be attacked with strong troops, yet it also is not sufficient to become a border trouble and may be planned for later; wait for the opportune moment and cut it down in one stroke to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bing is a foe that will fight to the death; it cannot be won by kindness and trust and must be crushed by a strong army, yet it is not enough of a border threat to demand immediate action—it can be left for later and struck down when the moment is ripe.

sentences.zh: 方今兵力精練，器用具備，群下知法，諸將用命。

translations.literal: At present military strength is refined and drilled, implements and equipment prepared, subordinates know the law, and generals obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Today our forces are well trained, arms and equipment ready, officials understand the law, and generals obey without question.

sentences.zh: 一稔之後，可以平邊，此歲夏秋，便可於沿邊貯納。

translations.literal: After one harvest year the borders can be pacified; this year's summer and autumn, stores can already be laid up along the borders.
translations.idiomatic: After one full year of preparation the frontiers can be pacified; this summer and autumn we should begin stockpiling supplies along the border.

sentences.zh: 臣書生也，不足以講大事，至於不達大體，不合機變，望陛下寬之。

translations.literal: Your servant is a mere scholar and is not sufficient to discuss great affairs; as for not grasping the larger pattern or not fitting opportune change, I hope Your Majesty will be indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a scholar and hardly qualified to discourse on great affairs; if I have failed to grasp the larger design or to suit changing circumstances, I beg Your Majesty's indulgence.

sentences.zh: 世宗覽之，愈重其器識。

translations.literal: Shizong read it and valued his capacity and insight all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong read the memorial and esteemed Pu's talent and judgment all the more highly.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷左諫議大夫，知開封府事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Remonstrator and given charge of Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Left Remonstrator and put in charge of the Kaifeng prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗以英武自任，喜言天下事，常憤廣明之後，中土日蹙，值累朝多事，尚未克復，慨然有包舉天下之志。

translations.literal: At first Shizong took upon himself martial valor, delighted in speaking of affairs under Heaven, and was often indignant that after the Guangming era the central lands daily shrank; encountering many affairs through successive reigns and still not having recovered them, he sighed with the ambition to embrace and lift up all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset Shizong prided himself on martial prowess and loved to discuss empire-wide affairs. He often raged that since the Guangming reign the heartland had steadily contracted; through reign after reign of turmoil the lost territories had not been recovered, and he burned with ambition to reunite the realm.

sentences.zh: 而居常計事者多不喻其旨，唯朴神氣勁峻，性剛決有斷，凡所謀畫，動愜世宗之意，由是急於登用。

translations.literal: Yet those who ordinarily deliberated on affairs mostly did not understand his intent; only Pu's spirit and bearing were forceful and stern, his nature firm, decisive, and resolute, and whatever he planned and designed invariably satisfied Shizong's mind, whereupon he was urgently advanced to employment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the officials who routinely advised him often missed his meaning; only Pu, forceful in spirit and stern in manner, firm and decisive by nature, planned in ways that always matched Shizong's intent, and the emperor hastened to promote him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜左散騎常侍，充端明殿學士，知府如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Left Regular Attendant, made Academician of the Duanming Hall, and continued as prefect as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Regular Attendant and Academician of the Duanming Hall while retaining his post as prefect.

sentences.zh: 是時，初廣京城，朴奉命經度，凡通衢委巷，廣袤之間，靡不由其心匠。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was first being expanded; Pu received orders to plan and measure it, and among all main thoroughfares and side lanes, in breadth and length, nothing was not shaped by his mind as craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was then being enlarged for the first time; Pu directed the planning, and every avenue and alley, every dimension of the project, bore the stamp of his design.

sentences.zh: 及世宗南征，以朴為東京副留守，車駕還京，改戶部侍郎兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned south, Pu was made Deputy Protector of the Eastern Capital; when the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong marched south, Pu was left as Deputy Protector of the Eastern Capital; on the emperor's return he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷樞密使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Commissioner of Military Affairs with the acting rank of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 頃之，丁內艱，尋起復授本官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his mother; soon he was recalled from mourning and granted his former offices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went into mourning for his mother; he was soon recalled to service and restored to his former posts.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，世宗再幸淮甸，兼東京留守，京邑庶務，悉以便宜制之，比及入蹕，都下肅如也。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Shizong again visited the Huai region, and Pu concurrently served as Protector of the Eastern Capital; all miscellaneous affairs of the capital district were entirely decided at his discretion, and by the time of the imperial entry the capital was orderly indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of his fourth year Shizong again toured the Huai region, leaving Pu as Protector of the Eastern Capital with full discretion over capital affairs; by the time the emperor returned, the city was perfectly orderly.

sentences.zh: （《默記》引《閑談錄》云：朴性剛烈，大臣藩鎮皆憚之。

translations.literal: (The Silent Record cites the Idle Talks Record as saying: Pu's nature was fierce and unyielding, and great ministers and military governors all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: (The Silent Record cites the Idle Talks Record: Pu was fierce by nature, and senior ministers and military governors alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 世宗收淮南，俾朴留守。

translations.literal: When Shizong recovered Huainan, he had Pu remain as protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong conquered Huainan, he left Pu behind as protector.

sentences.zh: 時以街巷隘狹，例從展拆，朴怒鄉校弛慢，於通衢中鞭背數十，其人忿然嘆云：「宣補鄉虞候，豈得便從決。」

translations.literal: At the time, because the lanes and alleys were narrow and cramped, it was customary to expand and demolish accordingly; Pu was angry that a village school officer was lax and slow, and in the main thoroughfare flogged his back several tens of strokes; the man resentfully sighed, saying: "Once I am appointed village patrol officer, how can I be summarily punished at will?"
translations.idiomatic: The streets were being widened by demolition as usual; Pu, angered by a village school officer's slackness, had him flogged dozens of times in the public road. The man muttered resentfully, "When I'm made village patrol officer, you won't be able to punish me on the spot like this."

sentences.zh: 朴微聞之，命左右擒至，立斃於馬前。

translations.literal: Pu faintly heard it, ordered his attendants to seize him and bring him forth, and had him immediately beaten to death before his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Pu overheard this, had him seized, and had him beaten to death on the spot before his horse.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，笑謂近臣曰：「此大愚人，去王朴面前誇宣補鄉虞候，宜其死矣。」）〉

translations.literal: Shizong heard of it and, laughing, said to his close attendants: "This great fool went before Wang Pu and boasted that he would be appointed village patrol officer—no wonder he died.")〉
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong heard of it he laughed and told his close attendants, "What a fool—to boast before Wang Pu that he'd soon be village patrol officer. Small wonder he was killed.")〉

sentences.zh: 六年三月，世宗令樹斗門於汴口，不逾時而歸朝。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Shizong ordered a sluice gate planted at the Bian mouth and returned to court before the season had passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year Shizong ordered a sluice gate built at the Bian River mouth and returned to court within the season.

sentences.zh: 是日，朴方過前司空李穀之第，交談之頃，疾作而仆於座，遽以肩舁歸第，一夕而卒，時年四十有五。

translations.literal: That day Pu was just passing the residence of the former Minister of Works Li Gu; in the midst of conversation illness seized him and he collapsed on his seat; he was hastily carried home on shoulders, and within one night he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That day Pu happened to be visiting the former Minister of Works Li Gu; in mid-conversation he was stricken and collapsed. He was carried home at once and died that night, aged forty-five.

sentences.zh: （《默記》：王朴仕周世宗，制禮作樂，考定聲律，正星曆，修刑統，百廢俱起。

translations.literal: (The Silent Record: Wang Pu served Zhou Shizong, regulated rites and made music, examined and fixed pitch and law, corrected the stars and calendar, revised the penal code, and a hundred neglected tasks all arose together.
translations.idiomatic: (The Silent Record: Wang Pu served Emperor Shizong of Zhou, established rites and music, fixed pitch standards, corrected the calendar, revised the penal code, and revived a hundred neglected institutions.

sentences.zh: 又取三關，取淮南，皆朴為謀。

translations.literal: Again taking the Three Passes and taking Huainan—all were planned by Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The capture of the Three Passes and of Huainan as well were all his strategies.

sentences.zh: 然事世宗才四年耳，使假之壽考，安可量也。）〉

translations.literal: Yet he served Shizong only four years; had he been granted long life, how could it have been measured?)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yet he served Shizong only four years; had he lived longer, who can say what he might have achieved?)〉

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之駭愕，即時幸其第，及柩前，以所執玉鉞卓地而慟者數四。

translations.literal: Shizong, hearing it, was startled and dismayed, immediately visited his residence, and before the bier, striking the jade axe he held to the ground, mourned several times.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was shocked and grieved, went at once to Pu's house, and before the coffin struck the jade axe he carried to the ground and wept again and again.

sentences.zh: 贈賻之類，率有加等，優詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: Funerary gifts and the like were all increased by one grade, and by gracious edict he was posthumously granted Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary gifts were all raised a grade, and an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王侁傳》：朴卒，世宗幸其第，召見諸孤，以侁為東頭供奉官。）〉

translations.literal: (Biography of Wang Shen in the Song History: When Pu died, Shizong visited his residence, summoned and saw all the orphans, and made Shen an Eastern Head Palace Attendant.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Biography of Wang Shen in the History of Song: When Pu died, Shizong visited his home, summoned his orphaned children, and appointed Shen Eastern Head Palace Attendant.)〉

sentences.zh: 朴性敏銳，然傷於太剛，每稠人廣座之中，正色高談，無敢觸其鋒者，故時人雖服其機變而無恭懿之譽。

translations.literal: Pu's nature was keen and sharp, yet he suffered from being too unyielding; in every crowded hall and broad seat he spoke with stern countenance and lofty discourse, and none dared touch his edge, so men of the time though they admired his resourcefulness had no reputation of respectful gentleness for him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was quick and sharp-witted, but excessively harsh; in any public gathering he spoke with stern countenance and forceful tone, and none dared cross him, so contemporaries respected his cleverness but never praised his courtesy.

sentences.zh: 其筆述之外，多所該綜，至如星緯聲律，莫不畢殫其妙，所撰《大周欽天曆》及《律準》，並行於世。

translations.literal: Beyond his written compositions he comprehended many fields; as for the stars, pitch, and musical law, none failed to exhaust their subtlety, and the Great Zhou Imperial Heaven Calendar and Pitch Standards that he composed both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond his writings he mastered many fields; in astronomy and music theory he plumbed their depths, and his Great Zhou Imperial Heaven Calendar and Pitch Standards both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: （《默記》云：周世宗於禁中作功臣閣，畫當時大臣如李蒨、鄭仁誨之屬。

translations.literal: (The Silent Record says: Zhou Shizong in the forbidden precincts built a Meritorious Ministers Pavilion and painted the great ministers of the time such as Li Qian and Zheng Renhui and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: (The Silent Record: Emperor Shizong of Zhou built a Meritorious Ministers Pavilion in the palace and painted portraits of leading officials such as Li Qian and Zheng Renhui.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，一日過功臣閣，風開半門，正與朴象相對，太祖望見，卻立聳然，整禦袍襟帶，磬折鞠躬。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, one day passing the Meritorious Ministers Pavilion, the wind opened half the door and he was directly facing Pu's image; Taizu looked and saw it, drew back and stood erect with awe, straightened his imperial robe, collar, and belt, bowed deeply with folded arms, and bent in obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu took the throne, he once passed the pavilion; a gust blew the door half open so that he faced Pu's portrait directly. Taizu stopped short in awe, straightened his imperial robe and belt, and bowed deeply.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「陛下貴為天子，彼前朝之臣，禮何過也？」

translations.literal: Those at his side said: "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven; he was a minister of the former dynasty—why is the ritual excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "Your Majesty is the Son of Heaven; he was only a minister of the previous dynasty—why such excessive courtesy?"

sentences.zh: 太祖以手指禦袍云：「此人在，朕不得此袍著。」

translations.literal: Taizu pointed with his finger at his imperial robe and said: "While this man was alive, I could not wear this robe."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu pointed at his robe and said, "While this man lived, I could not have worn this robe."

sentences.zh: 其敬畏如此。

translations.literal: His reverence and awe were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his reverence for him.

sentences.zh: 《五代史闕文》：周顯德中，朴與魏仁浦俱為樞密使。

translations.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: In the Xiande era of Zhou, Pu and Wei Renpu were both Commissioners of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: In the Xiande era, Pu and Wei Renpu both served as Commissioners of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時太祖皇帝已掌禁兵，一日，有殿直乘馬誤沖太祖導從，太祖自詣密地，訴其無禮。

translations.literal: At that time the future Taizu already commanded the forbidden army; one day a palace guard on horseback by mistake charged into Taizu's escort, and Taizu himself went to the secretariat to complain of the discourtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The future Taizu already commanded the palace guard; one day a palace guard on horseback accidentally rode into his procession, and Taizu went in person to the Military Affairs office to complain of the insult.

sentences.zh: 仁浦令徽院勘詰，朴謂太祖曰：「太尉名位雖高，未加使相。

translations.literal: Renpu ordered the Palace Service to investigate and question; Pu said to Taizu: "The Grand Marshal's name and rank, though high, have not yet been raised to commissioner and chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Renpu ordered an inquiry; Pu told Taizu, "Your rank as Grand Marshal is high, but you have not yet been made commissioner and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 殿直，廷臣也，與太尉比肩事主，太尉況帶職，不宜如此。」

translations.literal: A palace guard is a court minister who serves the ruler shoulder to shoulder with the Grand Marshal; the Grand Marshal moreover holds concurrent office—this should not be done thus."
translations.idiomatic: A palace guard is a court officer who serves the throne on equal footing with you; moreover you hold a concurrent post—you should not act this way."

sentences.zh: 太祖唯唯而出。

translations.literal: Taizu murmured assent and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu murmured agreement and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按，朴之行事，傳於人口者甚眾，而史氏缺書。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes that Pu's deeds, transmitted among men's mouths, are very numerous, yet the historians' records lack them.
translations.idiomatic: I note that Pu's deeds, widely known by word of mouth, are numerous, yet the official histories omit them.

sentences.zh: 臣聞重修《太祖實錄》，已於《李蒨傳》中見朴遺事，今復補其大者。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the revision of the Veritable Records of Taizu, remnants concerning Pu were already seen in the biography of Li Qian; now the greater ones are again supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that in the revised Veritable Records of Taizu, some anecdotes about Pu already appear in the biography of Li Qian; here I supplement the more important ones.

sentences.zh: 況太祖、太宗在位，每稱朴有上輔之器，朝列具聞。）〉

translations.literal: Moreover, while Taizu and Taizong were on the throne, each often said that Pu had the capacity of a chief minister, and the court ranks all heard it.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under Taizu and Taizong each often declared that Pu had the makings of a chief minister, as the whole court knew.)〉

sentences.zh: 楊凝式

translations.literal: Yang Ningshi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ningshi

sentences.zh: 楊凝式，華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Ningshi was a native of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ningshi came from Huayin.

sentences.zh: （《遊宦紀聞》載《凝式年譜》云：唐咸通十四年癸巳，凝式是年生，故題識多自稱癸巳人。

translations.literal: (Records of Travel and Official Service carries the Ningshi Chronological Record, saying: In the guisi year, the fourteenth year of Xiantong of Tang, Ningshi was born that year, so inscriptions often call themselves persons of guisi.
translations.idiomatic: (Records of Travel and Official Service records the Ningshi Chronological Record: He was born in 873, the guisi year of the Xiantong era, and often signed his works as a man of guisi.

sentences.zh: 又，《別傳》云：凝式，字景度。）〉

translations.literal: Again, the Separate Biography says: Ningshi, styled Jingdu.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Separate Biography also gives his style as Jingdu.)〉

sentences.zh: 父涉，唐末梁初，再登臺席，罷相守左僕射卒。

translations.literal: His father She, at the end of Tang and the beginning of Liang, twice ascended the council seat, and after leaving the chancellorship guarded the post of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat until death.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang She twice reached the chancellorship at the end of Tang and the beginning of Liang, then retired as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and died in that post.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史·楊涉傳》云：祖收，父嚴。

translations.literal: (Biography of Yang She in Ouyang's History says: grandfather Shou, father Yan.
translations.idiomatic: (Biography of Yang She in Ouyang Xiu's History names his grandfather as Shou and his father as Yan.

sentences.zh: 吳縝《纂誤》云：收與嚴乃兄弟，非父子也。

translations.literal: Wu Zhen's Collected Corrections says: Shou and Yan were brothers, not father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen's Collected Corrections notes that Shou and Yan were brothers, not father and son.

sentences.zh: 又，《遊宦紀聞》載《楊氏家譜》云：唐修行楊氏，系出越公房，本出中山相結，次子繼生洛州刺史暉，暉生河間太守恩，恩生越恭公鈞，出居馮翊，至藏器徙潯陽。

translations.literal: Again, Records of Travel and Official Service carries the Yang Clan Genealogy, saying: The Yang clan of Tang's Xingxing lineage descended from the house of the Duke of Yue, originally from Zhongshan Xiangjie; the second son Ji begot Hui, Prefect of Luozhou; Hui begot En, Administrator of Hejian; En begot Jun, the Respectful Duke of Yue, who moved out to dwell in Fengyi; down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Travel and Official Service also gives the Yang Clan Genealogy: the Xingxing Yangs descended from the house of the Duke of Yue in Zhongshan; through Ji, Hui of Luozhou, En of Hejian, and Jun the Respectful Duke of Yue, who settled in Fengyi, down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 唐相楊收之父曰遺直，生四子，名皆從「又」，曰發、假、收、嚴，以四時為義，故發之子名皆從「木」，假之子從「火」，收之子從「金」，嚴之子從「水」。

translations.literal: The father of Tang chancellor Yang Shou was called Yizhi; he had four sons whose names all followed the "you" radical: Fa, Jia, Shou, and Yan, taking the four seasons as the meaning; therefore Fa's sons' names all followed "wood," Jia's sons followed "fire," Shou's sons followed "metal," and Yan's sons followed "water."
translations.idiomatic: The father of Tang chancellor Yang Shou was Yizhi, who had four sons named with the "you" radical—Fa, Jia, Shou, and Yan—after the four seasons; Fa's descendants used the wood radical, Jia's the fire radical, Shou's the metal radical, and Yan's the water radical.

sentences.zh: 嚴生涉，涉生凝式，而收乃藏器之兄、涉之伯也。

translations.literal: Yan begot She, She begot Ningshi, while Shou was the elder brother of Zangqi and the paternal uncle of She.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was She's father and She's son was Ningshi; Shou was the elder brother of Zangqi and She's uncle.

sentences.zh: 《新五代史記·唐六臣傳》乃以收為涉之祖、嚴之父，非也。）〉

translations.literal: The New History of the Five Dynasties' Record, Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers, makes Shou She's grandfather and Yan She's father, which is incorrect.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The New History of the Five Dynasties' Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers wrongly makes Shou She's grandfather and Yan his father.)〉

sentences.zh: 凝式體雖蕞眇，而精神穎悟，

translations.literal: Though Ningshi's physique was small and slight, his spirit was sharp and penetrating,
translations.idiomatic: Though slight in build, Ningshi was keen of mind,

sentences.zh: （《宣和書譜》云：凝式形貌寢侻，然精神矍然，要大於身。）〉

translations.literal: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Compendium says: Ningshi's form and appearance were slight and frail, yet his spirit was alert and vigorous, seeming greater than his body.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Compendium: Ningshi looked frail, yet his spirit was vigorous and seemed larger than his frame.)〉

sentences.zh: 富有文藻，大為時輩所推。

translations.literal: Rich in literary ornament, he was greatly esteemed by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was richly gifted in letters and highly esteemed by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗朝，登進士第，解褐授度支巡官，再遷秘書郎，直史館。

translations.literal: In the reign of Tang Zhaozong he passed the jinshi examination, left commoner's dress and was appointed Revenue Circuit Inspector, was twice transferred to Secretary, and served in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he took the jinshi degree, entered service as Revenue Circuit Inspector, was twice promoted to Secretary, and served in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 梁開平中，為殿中侍御史、禮部員外郎、三川守，齊王張宗奭見而嘉之，請以本官充留守巡官。

translations.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang he served as Attending Censor within the Palace, Vice Minister of Rites, and Administrator of the Three Rivers; the Prince of Qi Zhang Zongshi saw and praised him and requested that he fill his original office as Protector Circuit Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiping era of Liang he was Attending Censor, Vice Minister of Rites, and Administrator of the Three Rivers; Prince of Qi Zhang Zongshi admired him and asked that he serve as his protector's circuit inspector in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 梁相趙光裔素重其才，奏為集賢殿直學士，改考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Liang chancellor Zhao Guangyi had long valued his talent and memorialized him as Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then changed him to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Liang chancellor Zhao Guangyi had long valued his talent and had him appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 唐同光初，授比部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang of Tang he was granted Director of the Bureau of Review and Drafted Imperial Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tang Tongguang era he was made Director of the Bureau of Review with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋以心疾罷去，改給事中、史館修撰，判館事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was dismissed on account of heart illness, changed to Supervising Secretary and History Office Compiler, and judged office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned because of a mental disorder and was made Supervising Secretary and History Office compiler with charge of the office.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，拜中書舍人，復以心疾不朝而罷。

translations.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, and again was dismissed for heart illness and failure to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne he was made Secretariat Drafter, but again left office because of his disorder and failure to attend court.

sentences.zh: 長興中，歷右常侍、工戶二部侍郎，以舊恙免，改秘書監。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he successively served as Right Regular Attendant and Vice Ministers of the Works and Revenue Bureaus, was excused on account of old ailment, and was changed to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era he served as Right Regular Attendant and Vice Ministers of Works and Revenue, then retired because of his old complaint and was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qingtai era he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 唐末帝按兵於懷覃，凝式在扈從之列，頗以心恙喧嘩於軍寨，末帝以其才名，優容之，詔遣歸洛。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang held his army at Huaizhen, Ningshi was in the entourage column and rather often, on account of heart ailment, made uproar in the military camp; the Last Emperor, because of his talent and name, indulged him and by edict sent him back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor of Tang encamped at Huaizhen, Ningshi was in his retinue and often caused disturbances in camp because of his mental condition; the emperor indulged him for his reputation and ordered him back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，改太子賓客，尋以禮部尚書致仕，閑居伊、洛之間，恣其狂逸，多所幹忤，自居守以降，咸以俊才耆德，莫之責也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin he was changed to Guest of the Heir Apparent, and shortly retired as Minister of Rites; dwelling in leisure between Yi and Luo, he gave free rein to his wildness and license and often gave offense, yet from prefects and guards downward all regarded him as a man of outstanding talent and venerable virtue and none blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jin Tianfu era he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, then retired as Minister of Rites and lived between the Yi and Luo rivers, indulging his eccentric ways and often giving offense; yet from prefects downward all treated him as a gifted elder and none held him accountable.

sentences.zh: 晉開運中，宰相桑維翰知其絕俸，艱於家食，奏除太子少保，分司於洛。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era of Jin, chancellor Sang Weihan knew that his stipend had ceased and that he was hard pressed for household food, and memorialized to appoint him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with separate duty at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin Kaiyun era, Chancellor Sang Weihan learned that Ningshi had lost his salary and was struggling to feed his household; he memorialized to make him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with a post at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，歷少傅、少師。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han he successively served as Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han reign era Qianyou he served as Junior Tutor and then Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太祖總兵，凝式候於軍門，且以年老不任庶事上訴，太祖特為奏免之。

translations.literal: When Taizu took command of the army, Ningshi waited at the army gate and moreover memorialized that he was old and unfit for miscellaneous duties; Taizu specially memorialized to exempt him.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Taizu took command of the army, Ningshi waited at the camp gate and petitioned that age made him unfit for routine duties; Taizu had him specially excused by memorial.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，表求致政，尋以右僕射得請。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era he submitted a memorial requesting retirement from office, and shortly obtained it as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangshun era he petitioned to retire and soon received permission as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，改左僕射，又改太子太保，並懸車。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was changed to Left Vice Director, then again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and in both cases hung up his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiande era he was made Left Vice Director, then Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, retiring from each post.

sentences.zh: 元年冬，卒於洛陽，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year he died at Luoyang, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Luoyang in the winter of the first year, aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 凝式長於歌詩，

translations.literal: Ningshi excelled at songs and poetry,
translations.idiomatic: Ningshi excelled at lyric poetry,

sentences.zh: （《別傳》云：凝式詩什，亦多雜以詼諧，少從張全義辟，故作詩紀全義之德云：「洛陽風景實堪哀，昔日曾為瓦子堆。

translations.literal: (The Separate Biography says: Ningshi's poems also often mixed in humor; in youth he followed Zhang Quanyi in service, and therefore composed a poem commemorating Quanyi's virtue, saying: "Luoyang's scenery is truly pitiable; in former days it was a heap of tile yards.
translations.idiomatic: (The Separate Biography: Ningshi's verse often mixed in wit; in youth he had served Zhang Quanyi and wrote to commemorate his patron: "Luoyang's scenery is truly pitiable—in former days it was nothing but a heap of tile yards.

sentences.zh: 不是我公重葺理，至今猶自一堆灰。」

translations.literal: Had it not been for our lord's heavy rebuilding and ordering, even now it would still be a heap of ash."
translations.idiomatic: Had our lord not rebuilt it from the ground up, it would still be a heap of ashes today."

sentences.zh: 他類若此。

translations.literal: Others of this kind were like this.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote many poems in this vein.

sentences.zh: 張從恩尹洛，凝式自汴還，時飛蝗蔽日，偶與之俱，凝式先以詩寄曰：「押引蝗蟲到洛京，合消郡守遠相迎。」

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en was Intendant of Luoyang; Ningshi returned from Bian, and at the time flying locusts darkened the sun; by chance he traveled with him, and Ningshi first sent a poem saying: "Escorting and leading locusts to the capital of Luo—the prefect ought to come far to welcome them."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong'en was intendant of Luoyang, Ningshi returned from Bian while locusts blotted out the sun; traveling together by chance, Ningshi sent ahead a poem: "Escorting locusts to the Luo capital—the prefect ought to ride far out to welcome them."

sentences.zh: 從恩弗怪也。

translations.literal: Cong'en did not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en was not offended.

sentences.zh: 然凝式詩句自佳，其題壁有「院似禪心靜，花如覺性圓」，清麗可喜。）〉

translations.literal: Yet Ningshi's poetic lines were themselves fine; on a wall he inscribed "The courtyard is like a Chan mind at rest, flowers like awakened nature made round," clear and lovely and delightful.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ningshi's own verse could be fine; on one wall he wrote, "The courtyard rests like a Chan mind; flowers bloom round like awakened nature"—lines clear, lovely, and delightful.)〉

sentences.zh: 善於筆劄，洛川寺觀藍墻粉壁之上，題紀殆遍，時人以其縱誕，有「風子」之號焉。

translations.literal: He was skilled at brush letters; on the blue walls and whitewashed surfaces of Luochuan's temples and shrines, inscriptions and records were nearly everywhere, and men of the time, because of his wild license, gave him the sobriquet "Madman."
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled with the brush; he left inscriptions on nearly every monastery wall in the Luoyang region, and contemporaries called him the "Madman" for his eccentric ways.

sentences.zh: （《別傳》云：凝式雖仕歷五代，以心疾閑居，故時人目以「風子」。

translations.literal: (The Separate Biography says: Though Ningshi served through the Five Dynasties, because of heart illness he dwelt in leisure, and therefore men of the time regarded him as the "Madman."
translations.idiomatic: (The Separate Biography: Though Ningshi served through five dynasties, he lived in retirement because of his mental disorder, and contemporaries called him the "Madman."

sentences.zh: 其筆跡遒放，宗師歐陽詢與顏真卿，而加以縱逸。

translations.literal: His brush traces were forceful and free; he took Ouyang Xun and Yan Zhenqing as masters and added to them wild abandon.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy was bold and free, modeled on Ouyang Xun and Yan Zhenqing but with an added wildness.

sentences.zh: 既久居洛，多遨遊佛道祠，遇山水勝概，輒留連賞詠，有垣墻圭缺處，顧視引筆，且吟且書，若與神會，率寶護之。

translations.literal: Having long dwelt in Luo, he often roamed Buddhist and Daoist shrines; encountering fine landscapes of mountains and waters, he would linger in appreciation and chanting; where there were broken walls and chipped corners, he would look back, take up the brush, chant and write together, as if meeting with spirit, and generally treasured and protected these works.
translations.idiomatic: Long settled in Luoyang, he wandered Buddhist and Daoist temples; at any fine landscape he would linger to admire and compose; wherever he found a broken wall he would turn, take up the brush, chant and write as if possessed, and people treasured whatever he left.

sentences.zh: 其號或以姓名，或稱癸巳人，或稱楊虛白，或稱希維居士，或稱關西老農。

translations.literal: His sobriquets were sometimes his surname and given name, sometimes "Man of guisi," sometimes "Yang the Empty White," sometimes "Layman Xiwi," sometimes "Old Farmer of Guanxi."
translations.idiomatic: He signed himself by his name, or as "Man of guisi," "Yang the Empty White," "Layman Xiwi," or "Old Farmer of Guanxi."

sentences.zh: 其所題後，或真或草，不可原詰，而論者謂其書自顏中書後一人而已。

translations.literal: After what he inscribed, whether regular or cursive script, it could not be traced to its origin, yet critics said that in calligraphy since Yan the Secretariat Director there was only this one man.
translations.idiomatic: His inscriptions, in regular or cursive script, were often indecipherable, yet critics held that since Yan Zhenqing there had been only one calligrapher his equal.

sentences.zh: 其佯狂之跡甚著，卜第於尹京之側，遇入府，前輿後馬，猶以為遲，乃策杖徒行，市人隨笑之。

translations.literal: His traces of feigned madness were very evident; he chose a residence beside the capital intendant's seat; when he happened to enter the prefectural office, with carriage before and horses behind he still thought it slow, and therefore walked alone with staff in hand, and market people followed laughing at him.
translations.idiomatic: His feigned madness was notorious; he built a house near the capital prefect's seat; even when visiting the prefecture with carriage and escort he found it too slow and walked alone with a staff while townsfolk laughed behind him.

sentences.zh: 嘗迫冬，家人未挾纊，會有故人過洛，贈以綿五十兩、絹百端，凝式悉留之修行尼舍，俾造襪以施崇德、普明兩寺飯僧，其家雖號寒啼饑，而凝式不屑屑也。

translations.literal: Once as winter approached, his household had not yet put on cotton; it happened that an old friend passing through Luo gave him fifty liang of cotton and a hundred bolts of silk; Ningshi entirely left them at the Xingxing nunnery, ordering socks made to supply meals for monks at the Chongde and Puming temples, and though his family though cried out with cold and hunger, Ningshi paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Once as winter neared his family had no cotton padding; an old friend passing through gave him fifty liang of cotton and a hundred bolts of silk, which Ningshi gave entirely to a nunnery to make socks for monks at the Chongde and Puming temples; though his household shivered and starved, he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 留守聞其事，乃自制衣給米遺之，凝式笑謂家人曰：「我固知留守必見赒也。」

translations.literal: The Protector heard of the matter and thereupon himself made clothes and gave rice as a gift; Ningshi laughed and told his household: "I knew all along the Protector would surely come to relieve us."
translations.idiomatic: The Protector heard of this and sent clothes and rice; Ningshi laughed and told his family, "I knew the Protector would surely send relief."

sentences.zh: 每旦起將出，仆請所之，楊曰：「宜東遊廣愛寺。」

translations.literal: Each morning when he rose and was about to go out, a servant asked where he was going; Yang said: "It is fitting to tour Guang'ai Temple to the east."
translations.idiomatic: Each morning as he set out, a servant asked his destination; Yang said, "Today we should visit Guang'ai Temple to the east."

sentences.zh: 仆曰：「不若西遊石壁寺。」

translations.literal: The servant said: "Better to tour Shibi Temple to the west."
translations.idiomatic: The servant said, "Better to visit Shibi Temple to the west."

sentences.zh: 凝式舉鞭曰：「姑遊廣愛。」

translations.literal: Ningshi raised his whip and said: "For the present, tour Guang'ai."
translations.idiomatic: Ningshi raised his whip and said, "For now, Guang'ai it is."

sentences.zh: 仆又以石壁為請，凝式乃曰：「姑遊石壁。」

translations.literal: The servant again requested Shibi, and Ningshi then said: "For the present, tour Shibi."
translations.idiomatic: The servant again urged Shibi, and Ningshi then said, "For now, Shibi it is."

sentences.zh: 聞者拊掌。

translations.literal: Those who heard clapped their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners clapped in delight.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：楊凝式父涉為唐宰相。

translations.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Ningshi's father She was a Tang chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Yang Ningshi's father She had been a Tang chancellor.

sentences.zh: 太祖之篡唐祚也，涉當送傳國璽，時凝式方冠，諫曰：「大人為宰相，而國家至此，不可謂之無過，而更手持天子印綬以付他人，保富貴，其如千載之後云云何？

translations.literal: When Taizu usurped the Tang mandate, She was to deliver the dynastic seal; at that time Ningshi had just come of age and remonstrated, saying: "Father, as chancellor, yet the state has come to this—one cannot say there is no fault; moreover to again hold the Son of Heaven's seals and cords in hand and deliver them to another to preserve wealth and honor—what will be said a thousand years hence?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu seized the Tang throne, She was to deliver the imperial seal; Ningshi, just come of age, remonstrated: "Father, as chancellor you cannot be blameless that the state has come to this; how can you hand the Son of Heaven's seal to another to save your wealth—what will posterity say?

sentences.zh: 其宜辭免之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting that you decline and be excused."
translations.idiomatic: You ought to refuse the commission."

sentences.zh: 時太祖恐唐室大臣不利於己，往往陰使人來探訪群議，搢紳之士及禍甚眾，涉常不自保，忽聞凝式言，大駭曰：「汝滅吾族。」

translations.literal: At that time Taizu feared that Tang great ministers were not favorable to himself and often secretly sent men to investigate group opinion; gentry and officials who met calamity were very numerous; She often could not preserve himself; suddenly hearing Ningshi's words, he was greatly alarmed and said: "You will destroy my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then feared Tang ministers and secretly sent agents to sound opinion; many officials perished; She lived in constant fear. Hearing Ningshi's words he cried, "You will destroy our whole clan!"

sentences.zh: 於是神色沮喪者數日。

translations.literal: Thereupon his expression was dejected for several days.
translations.idiomatic: He was dejected for days afterward.

sentences.zh: 凝式恐事泄，即日遂佯狂，時人謂之「楊風子」也。）〉

translations.literal: Ningshi feared the matter would leak out and that very day feigned madness; men of the time called him "Yang the Madman.")〉
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Ningshi that same day began feigning madness, and people called him "Yang the Madman.")〉

sentences.zh: 薛仁謙

translations.literal: Xue Renqian
translations.idiomatic: Xue Renqian

sentences.zh: 薛仁謙，字守訓，代居河東，近世徙家於汴，今為浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Xue Renqian, styled Shouxun, for generations dwelt in Hedong; in recent times the family moved to Bian, and he is now a native of Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Renqian, styled Shouxun, was of a Hedong family that in recent generations had moved to Bian; he was a native of Junyi.

sentences.zh: 父延魯，仕唐為汝州長史，累贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Yanlu served Tang as Administrator of Ruzhou and was repeatedly posthumously granted Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanlu had served Tang as Administrator of Ruzhou and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 仁謙謹厚廉恪，深通世務，梁鄴王羅紹威甚重之，累署府職。

translations.literal: Renqian was prudent, substantial, incorruptible, and scrupulous, deeply versed in worldly affairs; the Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei greatly valued him and repeatedly appointed him to prefectural posts.
translations.idiomatic: Renqian was prudent, honest, and deeply versed in affairs of state; Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei valued him highly and repeatedly gave him posts in his administration.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗即位於魏，授通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong ascended the throne at Wei, he was granted Herald.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang took the throne at Wei, Renqian was appointed Herald.

sentences.zh: 梁開平中，三聘於吳，得使者之體。

translations.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang he was thrice sent on missions to Wu and grasped the deportment of an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liang Kaiping era he went on three missions to Wu and mastered the conduct expected of an envoy.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉少卿、引進副使，累加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Deputy Commissioner of Presentation, and cumulatively added Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Deputy Commissioner of Presentation, with the acting rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 長興中，轉客省使、鴻臚少卿，出為建雄軍節度副使，進階光祿大夫、檢校左僕射，改光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he was changed to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, went out as Military Governor's Deputy of the Jianxiong Army, advanced in rank to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and was changed to Vice Minister of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era he became Commissioner of the Guest Bureau and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then Military Governor's Deputy of the Jianxiong Army, advancing to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, then Vice Minister of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，授檢校司空、河中節度副使，歸朝為衛尉、太僕二卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin he was granted Acting Minister of Works and Military Governor's Deputy of Hezhong; returning to court he served as the two ministers of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Court of the Imperial Stud respectively.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jin Tianfu era he was made Acting Minister of Works and Military Governor's Deputy of Hezhong; on returning to court he held the two directorships of the imperial stud offices.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，居喪制滿，授司農卿。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his stepmother; when the mourning period was complete he was granted Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his stepmother he was appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han he retired from office in his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han reign era Qianyou he retired in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 周初，改太子賓客致仕，仍加檢校司徒，進封侯爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was changed to Guest of the Heir Apparent in retirement, and still added Acting Minister of Education, advancing in enfeoffment to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou he retired as Guest of the Heir Apparent, was given the acting rank of Minister of Education, and was enfeoffed as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年冬，以疾終，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande he died of illness, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the winter of the third Xiande year, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，仁謙隨莊宗入汴也，有舊第為梁朝六宅使李賓所據，時賓遠適，而仁謙復得其第。

translations.literal: At first, when Renqian followed Zhuangzong into Bian, there was an old residence occupied by Li Bin, Liang's Commissioner of the Six Residences; at the time Bin was far away on assignment, and Renqian recovered his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Renqian followed Zhuangzong into Bian, his old residence had been taken by Li Bin, Liang's Commissioner of the Six Residences; Bin was away on assignment, and Renqian recovered the house.

sentences.zh: 或告云，賓之家屬厚藏金帛在其第內，仁謙立命賓親族盡出所藏而後入焉。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Bin's household had heavily stored gold and silk within the residence; Renqian immediately ordered Bin's kin to bring out all stored goods before he entered.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Bin's family had hidden gold and silk in the house; Renqian ordered Bin's relatives to remove everything before he would enter.

sentences.zh: 論者美之。

translations.literal: Commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 子居正，皇朝門下侍郎平章事。

translations.literal: His son Juzheng was Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor of the present dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juzheng became Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor under the present dynasty.

sentences.zh: 蕭願，字惟恭，梁宰相頃之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuan, styled Weigong, was the son of Liang chancellor Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuan, styled Weigong, was the son of the Liang chancellor Xiao Qing.

sentences.zh: 頃，明宗朝終於太子少保，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: Qing ended his career in the Mingzong reign as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the Tang History has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: Qing ended his career under Emperor Mingzong as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the History of Tang records his biography.

sentences.zh: 初，願之曾祖仿，唐僖宗朝入相，接客之次，願為兒童戲，效傳呼之聲。

translations.literal: At first Yuan's great-grandfather Fang entered the chancellorship in the reign of Tang Xizong; while receiving guests, Yuan as a child played, imitating the sound of heralds calling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's great-grandfather Fang had entered the chancellorship under Emperor Xizong of Tang; once while receiving guests, the child Yuan played at imitating the heralds' calls.

sentences.zh: 仿謂客曰：「余豈敢以得位而喜，所幸奕世壽考，吾今又有曾孫在目前矣。」

translations.literal: Fang said to the guest: "How would I dare rejoice at obtaining position? What I am fortunate in is generations of longevity; I now again have a great-grandson before my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Fang told his guest, "I dare not rejoice merely at gaining office; my fortune is generations of long life—and now I have a great-grandson before me."

sentences.zh: 願弱冠舉進士第，解褐為校書郎，改畿尉、直史館、監察殿中侍御史，遷比部員外郎、右司郎中、太常少卿。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years Yuan passed the jinshi examination, left commoner's dress as Collator, was changed to Capital District Assistant Magistrate, served in the History Office, became Investigating Attending Censor within the Palace, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Review, Right Department Director, and Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan passed the jinshi in early manhood, entered service as Collator, then Capital District Assistant Magistrate, History Office compiler, and Investigating Attending Censor, and rose to Vice Director of the Bureau of Review, Right Department Director, and Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝祀太微宮，願醉預公卿之列，為御史所彈，左遷右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the Mingzong reign, when sacrificing at the Taiwei Palace, Yuan was drunk and joined the ranks of dukes and ministers; he was impeached by the censor and demoted to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During a Mingzong-era sacrifice at the Taiwei Palace, Yuan appeared drunk among the chief ministers; the censor impeached him and he was demoted to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授兵部郎中，復金紫。

translations.literal: Before long he was granted Director of the Bureau of War and again received gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Director of the Bureau of War and again awarded the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服闋，自左司郎中拜右諫議大夫，歷給事中、右常侍、秘書監，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when mourning was complete, from Right Department Director he was appointed Right Remonstrator, successively served as Supervising Secretary, Right Regular Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat, and was changed to Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was promoted from Right Department Director to Right Remonstrator, then Supervising Secretary, Right Regular Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat, and finally Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年春卒。

translations.literal: He died in the spring of the first year of Guangshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of the first Guangshun year.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 願性純謹，承事父母，未嘗不束帶而見。

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was pure and careful; in serving his parents he never failed to wear his belt when meeting them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was pure and dutiful; he never visited his parents without being fully dressed.

sentences.zh: 然性嗜酒無節，職事弛慢。

translations.literal: Yet his nature loved wine without restraint, and official duties were lax and slow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he drank without restraint and was slack in his duties.

sentences.zh: 為兵部郎中日，常掌告身印，覃恩之次，頗怠職司，父頃為吏部尚書，代願視印篆，其散率如此。

translations.literal: When he was Director of the Bureau of War he often held charge of the commission seal; at times of broad grace he was quite negligent in office; his father Qing was Minister of the Civil Service and substituted for Yuan in inspecting the seal impressions—his looseness was thus.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of the Bureau of War he often held the commission seal; during general amnesties he was notably negligent, and his father Qing, then Minister of the Civil Service, had to inspect the seals for him—such was his carelessness.

sentences.zh: 願卒時年七十餘，其母猶在，一門壽考，人罕及者。

translations.literal: When Yuan died he was over seventy, and his mother was still alive; one household's longevity was rarely matched.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan died in his seventies while his mother still lived—a family's longevity rarely equaled.

sentences.zh: 盧損，其先范陽人也，近世任於嶺表。

translations.literal: Lu Sun—his ancestors were from Fanyang; in recent times they served in Lingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sun was of Fanyang ancestry; in recent generations his family had served in the far south.

sentences.zh: 父穎，遊宦於京師。

translations.literal: His father Ying pursued office while traveling and was at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying had pursued office and lived in the capital.

sentences.zh: 損少學為文，梁開平初，舉進士，惟頗剛介，以高情遠致自許。

translations.literal: Sun in youth studied literary composition; at the beginning of Kaiping of Liang he passed the jinshi examination, being only rather firm and upright, and took high sentiment and far-reaching purpose upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun studied letters in youth; in the early Liang Kaiping era he passed the jinshi examination. He was stiffly upright and prided himself on lofty detachment.

sentences.zh: 與任贊、劉昌素、薛鈞、高總同年擢第，所在相詬，時人謂之「相罵榜」。

translations.literal: With Ren Zan, Liu Changsu, Xue Jun, and Gao Zong he passed the examination in the same year; wherever they were they reviled one another, and men of the time called it the "Mutual Abuse List."
translations.idiomatic: He graduated the same year as Ren Zan, Liu Changsu, Xue Jun, and Gao Zong; they abused one another wherever they met, and contemporaries called their class list the "Mutual Abuse List."

sentences.zh: 及任贊、劉昌素居要切之地，而損自異，不相親狎。

translations.literal: When Ren Zan and Liu Changsu occupied critical positions, Sun set himself apart and was not intimate with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Zan and Liu Changsu rose to key posts, Sun kept his distance and would not be friendly with them.

sentences.zh: 時左丞李琪素薄劉昌素之為人，常善待損。

translations.literal: At the time Left Vice Director Li Qi had long looked down on Liu Changsu's conduct and often treated Sun well.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Li Qi had long despised Liu Changsu's character and often treated Sun kindly.

sentences.zh: 琪有女弟眇，長年婚對不售，乃以妻損，損慕琪聲稱納之，及琪為輔相，致損仕進。

translations.literal: Qi had a younger sister who was blind; for many years no marriage match succeeded, and he therefore gave her to Sun as wife; Sun, admiring Qi's reputation, accepted her, and when Qi became chief minister he caused Sun to advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had a blind younger sister long unmarried; he gave her to Sun in marriage, and Sun, admiring Qi's reputation, accepted. When Qi became chief minister he advanced Sun's career.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，累遷至右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era of Liang he was repeatedly transferred up to Right Department Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liang Zhenming era he rose to Right Department Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 唐天成初，由兵部郎中、史館修撰轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng of Tang, from Director of the Bureau of War and History Office Compiler he was changed to Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tang Tiancheng era he moved from Director of the Bureau of War and History Office compiler to Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 屢上書言事，詞理淺陋，不為名流所知。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs; his wording and reasoning were shallow and crude, and he was not known among leading figures.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly on public affairs, but his reasoning was shallow and leading figures took no notice of him.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，盧文紀作相，密與損參議時政。

translations.literal: In Qingtai, Lu Wenji became chancellor and secretly deliberated current policy with Sun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era Chancellor Lu Wenji privately consulted Sun on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，長興中，唐末帝鎮河中，損嘗為加恩使副，及末帝即位，用為御史中丞。

translations.literal: At first, in Changxing, the Last Emperor of Tang was stationed at Hezhong; Sun once served as deputy to the Grace-bestowing Commissioner, and when the Last Emperor ascended the throne, he was employed as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Changxing era, the Last Emperor of Tang held Hezhong; Sun had served as deputy grace commissioner, and when the emperor took the throne he made Sun Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 拜命之日，以自前憲司不能振舉綱領，俾風俗頹壞，乃大為條奏，而有「平明放鑰，日出守端」之語，大為士人嗤鄙。

translations.literal: On the day he received appointment, because he himself [said that] the former censorate could not raise and uphold the guiding principles, causing customs to decay and collapse, he therefore made great itemized memorials, and there were the words "At dawn release the locks, at sunrise guard rectitude," which were greatly mocked and despised by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he declared that the censorate had failed to uphold standards and customs had decayed, and issued a long list of regulations including "Unlock at dawn, guard rectitude at sunrise"—much ridiculed by scholars.

sentences.zh: 有頃，誤詳赦書，失出罪人，停任。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he erred in reviewing the amnesty edict and released a criminal by mistake; his office was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he misread an amnesty edict and wrongly released a criminal; he was suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，復為右散騎常侍，轉秘書監，大失所望，即拜章辭位，乃授戶部尚書致仕，退居潁川。

translations.literal: In Tianfu of Jin he again became Right Regular Attendant, was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, was greatly disappointed in his hopes, immediately submitted a memorial resigning office, and was thereupon granted Minister of Revenue in retirement, withdrawing to live at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin Tianfu era he was again Right Regular Attendant, then Director of the Secretariat; deeply disappointed, he resigned at once and retired as Minister of Revenue, withdrawing to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 時少保李鏻年將八十，善服氣導引，損以鏻之遐齡有道術，酷慕之。

translations.literal: At the time Junior Guardian Li Lin was nearly eighty, skilled in ingesting qi and guiding exercises; Sun, because of Lin's advanced age and possession of the Way's techniques, ardently admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Guardian Li Lin was then nearly eighty and skilled in breath cultivation; Sun greatly admired his longevity and arts of longevity.

sentences.zh: 仍以潁川逼於城市，乃卜居陽翟，誅茅種藥，山衣野服，逍遙於林圃之間，出則柴車鶴氅，自稱具茨山人。

translations.literal: Still considering Yingchuan too close to the city, he chose a residence at Yangzhai, cut thatch and planted medicine, wore mountain clothes and wild dress, roamed freely among groves and gardens, and when going out used a brushwood cart and crane cloak, calling himself the Mountain Man of Juci.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yingchuan still too near the city, he settled at Yangzhai, built a thatched hut, planted herbs, wore rustic dress, and wandered among woods and gardens; abroad he rode a brushwood cart in a crane cloak and called himself the Mountain Man of Juci.

sentences.zh: 晚年與同輩五六人，於大隗山中疏泉鑿坯為隱所，誓不復出山，久之，齒發不衰，似有所得。

translations.literal: In his later years with five or six peers of the same generation, in Mount Dawei he opened springs and cut earth to make a hermit's dwelling, swearing never again to leave the mountains; after a long time his teeth and hair did not decline, as if he had gained something.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he and five or six companions carved out a hermitage on Mount Dawei, vowing never to leave the hills; in time his teeth and hair showed no decline, as if he had found the Way.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年秋卒，時年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died in the autumn of the third year of Guangshun, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the autumn of the third Guangshun year, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王仁裕

translations.literal: Wang Renyu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renyu

sentences.zh: 王仁裕，字德輦，天水人。

translations.literal: Wang Renyu, styled Delian, was a native of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renyu, styled Delian, came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 少孤，不從師訓，年二十五，方有意就學。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he did not follow a teacher's instruction; at age twenty-five he first had the intention to pursue study.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he had no schooling; only at twenty-five did he begin to study in earnest.

sentences.zh: 一夕夢剖其腸胃，引西江水以浣之，又睹水中砂石，皆有篆文，因取而吞之。

translations.literal: One night he dreamed that his entrails were cut open, the waters of the Xijiang drawn to wash them, and again he saw sand and stones in the water all bearing seal script; he therefore took and swallowed them.
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed his bowels were opened and washed with the waters of the West River; he saw pebbles in the water inscribed with seal script and swallowed them.

sentences.zh: 及寤，心意豁然，自是資性絕高。

translations.literal: When he awoke his mind was open and clear; from then on his natural endowment was surpassingly high.
translations.idiomatic: On waking his mind was clear, and from then on his talent was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: （案：此下有闕文。

translations.literal: (Note: Below this there is missing text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Text is missing below this point.

sentences.zh: 《輿地紀勝》云：王仁裕知貢舉時，所取進士三十三人，皆一時名公卿，李昉、王溥為冠。）〉

translations.literal: Geographical Records of the Empire says: When Wang Renyu supervised the metropolitan examination, the thirty-three jinshi he selected were all famous dukes and ministers of the time, with Li Fang and Wang Pu at the head.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Geographical Records of the Empire: When Wang Renyu ran the metropolitan examination, the thirty-three jinshi he chose were all leading figures of the day, headed by Li Fang and Wang Pu.)〉

sentences.zh: 有詩萬餘首，勒成百卷，目之曰《西江集》，蓋以嘗夢吞西江文石，遂以為名焉。

translations.literal: He had more than ten thousand poems, carved into a hundred scrolls, titled the Collected Poems of the West River, because he had once dreamed of swallowing the West River's literary stones and therefore took this as its name.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than ten thousand poems, compiled in a hundred-scroll collection titled Collected Poems of the West River, named for his dream of swallowing the inscribed stones of the West River.

sentences.zh: （《輿地紀勝》：仁裕所著有《紫泥集》、《西江集》、《入洛記》，共百卷。）〉

translations.literal: (Geographical Records of the Empire: Works composed by Renyu include the Collected Purple Mud, Collected Poems of the West River, and Record of Entering Luo, one hundred scrolls in all.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Geographical Records of the Empire: Renyu's works included Collected Purple Mud, Collected Poems of the West River, and Record of Entering Luo—a hundred scrolls in all.)〉

sentences.zh: 後為兵部尚書、太子少保，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as Minister of War and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Minister of War and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, then died.

sentences.zh: 裴羽，字用化，唐僖宗時宰相贄之子也。

translations.literal: Pei Yu, styled Yonghua, was the son of chancellor Zan in the reign of Tang Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yu, styled Yonghua, was the son of Chancellor Pei Zan under Emperor Xizong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 羽少以父任為河南壽安尉。

translations.literal: Yu in youth, through his father's privilege, was made Assistant Magistrate of Shou'an in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yu entered office through his father's privilege as Assistant Magistrate of Shou'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 入梁，遷御史臺主簿，改監察御史。

translations.literal: Entering Liang, he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Censorate and changed to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he became Chief Clerk of the Censorate, then Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗時，為吏部郎中，使於閩，遇颶風，飄至錢塘。

translations.literal: In the time of Tang Mingzong he was Director of the Bureau of the Civil Service and was sent as envoy to Min; he met a typhoon and was driven to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingzong of Tang he was Director of the Bureau of the Civil Service and sent as envoy to Min; a typhoon drove his ship to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 時安重誨用事，削奪吳越王封爵，羽被留於錢塘，經歲不得歸，後重誨死，後吳越復通中國，羽始得還。

translations.literal: At the time An Chonghui held power, stripped the King of Wuyue of his enfeoffment and rank; Yu was detained at Qiantang and for a full year could not return; afterward Chonghui died, and later Wuyue again communicated with the Central State, and Yu was then able to return.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui was then in power and stripped the King of Wuyue of his titles; Yu was detained at Qiantang for a year. After Chonghui's death Wuyue restored relations with the central court, and Yu was able to return.

sentences.zh: 晉初，累遷禮部侍郎、太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, he was repeatedly transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Jin he rose through repeated promotions to Vice Minister of Rites and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，為左散騎常侍，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalier-at-Arms and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he served as Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalier-at-Arms and died.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 羽之使閩也，正使陸崇卒於道，羽載其喪還，歸其橐裝，時人義之。

translations.literal: When Yu was envoy to Min, the chief envoy Lu Chong died on the road; Yu carried his coffin back and returned his baggage and belongings; men of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: On Yu's mission to Min the chief envoy Lu Chong died en route; Yu brought the body home and returned all his effects, for which contemporaries praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 段希堯

translations.literal: Duan Xiyao
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiyao

sentences.zh: 段希堯，河內人也。

translations.literal: Duan Xiyao was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiyao was from Henei.

sentences.zh: 祖約，定州戶掾，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Registrar of Households in Ding Prefecture; posthumously enfeoffed Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue served as a household registrar in Ding Prefecture and was posthumously made Vice Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父昶，晉州神山縣令，累贈太子少保。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Magistrate of Shenshan County in Jin Prefecture; repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang was magistrate of Shenshan County in Jin Prefecture and was posthumously promoted over time to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 希堯少有器局，累歷州縣。

translations.literal: Xiyao in youth had capacity and breadth of mind; he repeatedly passed through prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyao showed strong character and ability from youth and served in successive prefectural and county posts.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，為衛州錄事參軍，會晉高祖作鎮於鄴，聞其勤幹，奏改洺州糾曹。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng period of Tang he was Recording Secretary of Wei Prefecture; it happened that Jin Gaozu held his fief at Ye; hearing of his diligence and competence, he memorialized to change him to Investigating Officer of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era of Tang he was recording secretary for Wei Prefecture; when Jin Gaozu held his fief at Ye he heard of Xiyao's diligence and had him transferred to investigating officer for Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及晉祖鎮太原，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu governed at Taiyuan, he recruited him as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu governed from Taiyuan he took Xiyao onto his staff as an aide.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，晉祖總戎於代北，一日軍亂，遽呼萬歲，晉高祖惑之，希堯曰：「夫兵猶火也，弗戢將自焚。」
